title: What If Lightning Stopped Forever?

scenes.text: What if lightning stopped forever? The forests of the far north would feel it first.
Right now Earth sees about 44 lightning flashes every second. That's well over a billion a year.
In Alaska, lightning started about 95 percent of the area burned between 1975 and 2015.
Take the sparks away, and the northern forests, where nearly every wildfire is lit by lightning, would see far fewer fires.
Each flash also makes nitrogen oxides, about 10 percent of the world's supply, which help build ozone high in the sky.
Without it, the chemistry of the air shifts. The most feared moment in a storm quietly keeps Earth running.
